reviews.text: They turned Returnal into Megaman. That might not mean anything to you, but it means the world to me. Fast, fluid, fun, and I can't wait to play a ton more. I've been in a gaming slump recently and I didn't know what to play, but now I can't wait to fight all of the bosses and see what the rest of the guns and abilities do. The art is beautiful and the soundtrack is fantastic. Great job devs :) Edit: Definitely worth the purchase. It's just so much fun, I can't wait for all the content updates in the coming months.

Already completely in love with this game. Megaman influences and some Roboquest feel as well. Extremely well polished and stupid fun hectic, varied combat already. The few out of the many weapons I've used thus far are satisfying to shoot in every aspect, sound, design, feel, punchynes. The movement feels great and the punch execute is just fantastic every time, love the slight slowdown when you do use it to execute. Can't wait to sink plenty more hours into this

第一称爬塔游戏，目前测试游玩的缺点就是枪械手感不好，枪械打击反馈很差，每层区域怪物量很少但血量又很高，应该是我天赋没加高的原因吧，建议制作组可以增加一些人物手部动作，增强元素效果，增加怪物对元素伤害的反应，不过游戏本身的玩法我很喜欢，加油

你是信我这个20+小时通关，大部分内容解锁的玩家；还是信那些几小时都不到的评测 经过最近一次的更新，游戏的爽度有一个较大的提升，先是近战击杀敌人都会掉落护盾，让玩家有更好的体验，能越战越勇。第二，处决的击飞速度明显增快，敌人爆炸的范围也明显增大，让连环杀敌更高效，速通房间成为了可能！但我目前还不是很推荐，主要就是数值以及人物成长的解锁曲线，有着较大的问题 以下为游戏刚出时候的评测，数值方面仍未做调整。 不得不承认美术音乐不错，但音效略有些弱，关卡设计属于，敌人量少但血很多，感觉不如量多血少。前期，有时候打了3个怪，无法处决，也就不掉护盾，真的很难受。房间和房间之间的连接，多为跳跳乐，跳跳乐还有很多陷阱，一不注意，小半血就没了！ 总结：内容量不足，等正式版 一共两张图，3个BOSS，关底BOSS随机，每关敌人BUFF拉满，游戏中房间和房间的链接也有很多跳跳乐。 前2-3个小时纯坐牢时间，因为武器打BOSS很刮痧，打不掉BOSS就没法解锁核心，（核心的效果为增加一个反弹弹幕技能）没有反弹就打不动BOSS，开始循环。 像是武器回收，冲刺CD这种比较基础的能力，需要花几局的时间来解锁。 另外一方面，终结敌人的击飞方向居然和移动方向挂钩，而不是瞄准方向，也就是说，你想打出连锁伤害，还需要来个急停，再按对应的方向键，恕我脑子转不过来。且近战没有一定的辅助瞄准，偶尔会出现没打中的情况。 后期，一个技能打BOSS 3000血，CD也就几秒，一把武器DPS也就几百，这平衡数值略有些问题。

A fantastic Roguelite, with fluid mobility, very good variety of upgrades and weapons (each with their own perks), and a very colorful and distinguishable art style. Although it is early-access, so there are balancing and optimization problems, but the base is incredibly entertaining and complete. It's totally worth it. Esp: Un Roguelite fantástico, con una movilidad fluida, muy buena variedad de mejoras y armas (cada una con sus beneficios), y un estilo artístico muy colorido y distinguible. Aunque es early-access, por lo que existen problemas de balanceo y optimización, pero la base es increíblemente entretenida y completa. Vale totalmente la pena.

给新人写点小攻略 初期很坐牢，人物的基础功能全都没有（冲刺 蹬墙跳 背包自动换弹 初始核心这些），所以前期基本不能通关 ， 需要赚资源点天赋。密码云里 ，武器和技能全都不要点 ， 纯纯污染卡池 ，特别是武器 ，不能提升你局内的实力 ，反而全是一些你用了一次就不想拿第二次的渣渣 ，非要用的话只推荐点等离子卡宾枪（火步枪）和震颤（高伤害半自动自带穿透的2段震动手枪）， 其次技能 ， 技能的作用有限 ，一般只作为加BUFF的存在 ，所以把资源全投入到天赋里才能保证初期打败第一个BOSS拿到坚强主核心 ，比较重要的几个天赋是额外积分（开局带200钱），回收装备 ， 商店补货（刷新商店）， 尽快升满这些 ， 护盾供应这个天赋不要点 ，钱箱都被这个护盾占了，点了这个天赋一局下来少好几个核心升级 ， 局内3选1只拿核心升级，墙上的技能和武器全都不要买 ，留钱到商店买核心（一路赚下来的钱够在商店每轮买2、3个核心）。有了坚强主核心后 接下来是打败其他BOSS拿他们的主副核心，其他核心的亲密度并不是拿到了就能提升，需要在秘密基地拿到提升亲密度的功能才行（就是开局右侧那边，需要拿到蹬墙跳才能过去）。这个拿核心的顺序也有讲究，优先拿伏特核心，其次攻击核心，最后才拿飓风核心。新人只打得过第一层BOSS的情况下，不要打鸟人，虽然游戏没有难度分级，但是难度是会一直提升的，亲密度满了，BOSS技能就有变化，局内场景陷阱会额外增多增强，鸟人的飓风核心是4个核心里最渣的，而且飓风核心亲密度满了，场内就多了那些单向屏障极其恶心，这玩意怪的投射物能穿过去，你的投射物不能，你把这些屏障打破了，过一会又自动生成了，而且极其多，甚至战斗结束后还一直存在，想远距离打箱子都麻烦。初始坚强核心就是最强的，副核心选伏特核心（只需要他那个重型爆炸，能加爆发的范围），局内往死里升级核心，核心的伤害和等级挂钩，爆发这核心虽然介绍是反射敌人的投射物，但是他本身是能对碰到罩子的敌人造成伤害的，优先升巨型爆炸和重型爆炸，这样罩子能炸半张地图这么大的范围，满等级的爆发站地图中间一发Q就直接结束战斗了，其次反弹冲刺和重击反弹这些加满后，一个无CD的重击反射投射物能打个2000多伤害，过图都不用开枪。满级爆发打BOSS直接一个Q不反射都有4000伤害，10层狂怒直接8000伤害一发Q瞬秒BOSS，再看看飓风核心的大招猎鹰俯冲，满级猎鹰俯冲打BOSS造成高达60伤害的暴击！要你这60点伤害何用，还不如开枪打一发子弹呢，你这俯冲还没无敌，贴脸敌人伤害全吃，纯纯废物，飓风核心叠暴击BUFF只适合单发低射速的武器，例如筒子，暴击需要一直跳一直滞空来叠到10层，10层就是百分百暴击，每次暴击消耗一层，用筒子可以保证每次打出去一发后换弹期间可以继续叠暴击，当然也可以配搭攻击核心来主打步枪冲锋枪的输出，但是这样叠半天的暴击BUFF半轮弹夹就消耗完了，而且现在版本坚强核心和飓风核心还没双重组合。。。。反观攻击核心和伏特核心这2个都能和坚强核心相提比论，伏特当主核心，局内升满核心等级后，BOSS战开门后不要急着进去，在门口等CD扔3个伏特电球到BOSS会出现的位置，在扔第三个伏特球的瞬间冲进去，这时候BOSS动画出现，说一堆台词，在他说台词的时候3个伏特球就能一直电他对他造成伤害，动画还没播放完就能把他电死了。攻击核心这个没啥好说的，高等级后一个冲刺就能把小怪秒了，打BOSS冲刺5下开个大招再冲5下就结束战斗了，就是得配个坚强副核心拿个冲刺反射来保证安全。

有点玩腻了，重复度太高了，随机元素根本不够。局外成长因素，基本就是把demo里的展示环节给拆了，然后只有血和盾的成长，没有攻击力成长。 打怪慢的难受，第二关第三关开始，配的枪和技能词条不好，一个小怪都得打半天。 demo里的展示内容，全给拆了，拆成一个一个部分，在正式版去慢慢解锁。 真tm sb！ --------------------------------- 玩着感觉怪怪的.........我是先玩的demo试了下，感觉挺好玩，玩了一个多小时，买了个游戏。 结果正式游戏里，养成进程这些跟demo不一样，上来大招冲刺都没有。 核心也没有。 玩了两局，现在只有个冲刺，还是没大招，也没有主线对话进展，不知道要怎么解锁大招.....0. 而且感觉正式版游戏和demo不是同一个版本的，地图差距也挺多的。 再一个不继承demo进度，demo一个多小时白打，又得重头打，主要是那个粉色水晶给的真少。 前期解锁东西太慢了，我还没大招，也没有开局武器。 挺怪的。倒是可以再玩玩，至少希望有新东西，新武器新流派，不要只是两个demo里玩不了的新地图。 有些游戏喜欢把做的最好的放在demo里，正式服虽然多了武器流派但是不好玩，希望这个游戏不是这样。
- 蛮好玩的，打击感很棒，主打一个爽！ - 就是后面那个OS大Boss有点套公式了，打击薄弱点后一个重击然后回去窝着恢复后再出来打弱点。 - 前三关的小Boss都是一个区域内自由拼杀的很爽！ - 进去后不要被白绿蓝橙的武器颜色迷惑了，刚开始以为颜色代表品质，结果发现是对应的属性... 游戏内的可玩元素真的很多很多，但是希望能像以撒那样更新更多的Boss以及道具和玩法

Please don't make roguelites, make this genre disappear completely. I thought I was gonna spend hours of going through awesome levels, instead I spent like 4 hours dying in the same level. UPDATE: I have now played almost 20 hours and have made a little over 20 runs (each level can take around 30 minutes or more) and after all the powers I've gotten, all the things I've unlocked and purchased, I can still get my ass handed to me by the first boss. The game itself isn’t bad, with solid mechanics and engaging gameplay, but the overly stylized 'badass girly pink' theme didn’t appeal to me. It felt too dominant throughout the experience, making it hard to fully immerse myself. If you enjoy that aesthetic, you might love it, but for me, it was a major drawback.

+ The arena combat is top notch + The visuals are nice + Performance has been great on my 12900 & 3080ti - Bosses are kind of a bummer. All of the combat arenas are relatively large and multi level where movement is a blast, except the boss arenas. They are just flat, round and dull. The bosses are both spongy and capable of two or three shotting you. Not every boss needs to be a souls boss. I have a sneaking suspicion that the boss difficulty is why so few are playing this. - Parkour levels are pants. You have no feet, or any way of pinpointing where you're going to land. 1st person wall jump just doesn't work. - Let me decide if I want to make the game harder. After you beat the 1st boss the game's difficulty ramps up permanently. - Not a lot of content. Same handful of bosses, enemies, and stages. Maybe if there were more bosses they wouldn't need be so tanky. - About half of the weapons I've unlocked are just bad. They either don't shoot fast enough, don't do any damage, or both. The basic arena combat is a blast and the graphics are good, everything else needs work.

Look, I want to recomend this game, I do, at the core it is really fun having what is essentially doom but a roguelike, great concept, the way you get stronger, pretty unique. overall I like the core of this game. The problem is that the devs don't seem to know what difficulty is. which, quite honestly is really frustrating, ever since my first run its been an issue and its only gotten worse the more I play. Their idea of difficulty is to make the game more annoying, you know your shield? how about most enemies get attacks that ignore that and just deal 10 damage to your max HP, you know how your items and choices are key to this game? yea lets limit them as much as we can, and lets replace your weapon spawns with a health pack, something you will not need given the enemies are only going to kill you through removing your max HP anyways. And then you know how speed is the key part of the game? Yea, lets make sure everything takes much longer to complete, lets make half the enemies invulnereable untill you kill the other ones, does this make it hard? no, because you can just avoid them, you can walk away from the melee units, you can easily just dodge any shots fired, especially since you aren't focusing on actually shooting an enemy anymore and just circeling around the room to find whoever isn't invulnereable. I cannot in good faith actually recomend this game, despite how much I want to, simply because it doesn't have a difficulty, only a tedium modifier

很难说这个游戏的优势在哪，毕竟boss总共就四个，地图不算最终关也就四个区域，boss打掉给永久可以装备的核心类似于新的角色，但是算上自己初始自带的也就4个核心，主角个子很矮以至于射击的视角并不够高，要说城建城建也不存在只有各种各样的奖杯给你一个开阔独立的陈列室，机制方面，元素伤害类型算上动能一起总共也就四种，可重复游玩性也很难说，玩一把基本就不打算玩第二把。 但真要说优点的话，就这么说吧，再增加三个boss也就是附带三种核心，给家园增加一点可以用代笔购买的装饰以及hades同款的狗牌等级，家园里面增加一些从地图中解锁的可以互动的小动物，这游戏就能跟hades坐一桌了，打击感非常好，元素伤害种类较少也降低了搭配被污染或者很难找到想要的搭配之类的风险，boss提供的核心虽然说类似于角色，但是区分度很高的同时，核心之间能两两联动类似于吸血鬼幸存者的终极亦或者hades的双重祝福，其中风暴领主给的二段跳飞行搭配祝福玩起来真的有种我在学着飞行的体验感。 游戏本体难度不高，甚至可以说非常低，游戏前期会解锁一个词条叠加，允许玩家把捡到的武器词条给某一个装备栏位置，而有了词条游戏难度就会急剧降低，比如说拿攻城锤（单发散弹）拿最后一发子弹暴伤提高100%，暴击率之类的，亦或者最后一发子弹附带一发燃烧/振动/雷电/动能，亦或者就单独敌方拿受到某种元素伤害后受到伤害增加，这个数值大概是25%*5~75%*5，结合各种增益手段，甚至能一发带走满血精英或者几发弹药秒掉前期的boss，加上不错的打击感可以说非常爽，但是同理搭配完一局满足了就不想玩第二局。

This game just isn't any fun and there's basically no reason to play it over its competition. I wish I had something more insightful to say but a boomer-shooter should not be struggling *this much* to properly hook me. The main issue is a combination of the style and gameplay. The game's artstyle and music is more reminiscent of something like Megaman or Megaman X than any FPS. Battleshapers features bright colors, a plasticky shading to everything where robots look like action figures and guns look and sound like super soakers, and a soundtrack that goes for high pitched guitars over heavy bass (I don't know music theory but hopefully you know what I mean). The game's frequent cutscenes are comprised of slow, cheesy banter between characters. I appreciate what they tried with this artstyle, the effort and passion is on display, it's just that it completely sucks. I'd personally say that this is one of those moments where "nobody else is trying something like this" means "everyone else knew they shouldn't do this". The visuals and soundtrack of a sidescroller platformer meant for kids to play 8 feet away from the TV simply don't map onto an FPS for the PC. From this perspective the game is 90% a mangled ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of different particle effects and robot limbs, and the remaining 10% you can make out looks about as impressive as a beyblade commercial. By contrast, Roboquest has NONE of these issues because it uses tried-and-true FPS aesthetics like postapocolyptic sci-fi comics (I.E. Borderlands) to make the game have very strong readability and extremely satisfying weapons while still being a "Megaman FPS roguelike". For me, the smoking gun of the game's visuals having zero 'cool factor' is the classes. Unlike other games which offer an entirely new character to play, in Battleshapers you get to pick from 4 different balls. You can choose the white ball, the red ball, the purple ball, or the green ball. I can appreciate that the balls probably play differently and that there's a nifty system where you can equip a primary and secondary ball, but I frankly don't care because instead of unlocking crazy new characters you unlock ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BALLS. What's the point of playing if the crazy loot the devs are offering as a reward is 3 new ball PNGs instead of anything cool? The second issue is that the gameplay just isn't that fun. I'll try to stay modest since I haven't seen a ton of the game yet but from what I can tell Battleshapers has an upsetting combination of lacking any new ideas while also doing things worse than earlier games. The only way to recover your shield in BS is to use what's basically the Doom reboot's glory kill system- except a fair bit jankier since you need to use the short-ranged punch on glowing enemies to finish them off and there's no invincible finisher animation or leniency for accidentally shooting the glowing enemies instead of punching them. This is already a somewhat questionable decision since Doom and Doom: Eternal have arguably already been beaten by many indie shooters. Ultrakill and IMO also Turbo Overkill completely have the Doom reboot's number with their kill-to-heal systems. Not to mention the bain of Battleshapers' existance, Roboquest, proves that you can keep it simple. Just have enemies drop short-lived health pickups on kill, no weird finishers required. The real thing that makes BS extremely unimpressive is that its main roguelike competition, Deadlink, basically just has this system except it's actually good. Instead of completely gutting the flow of combat by forcing you to drop whatever you were doing to focus on punching glowing enemies, Deadlink both encourages you to play well and rewards you for doing so. Marking enemies with abilities and grenades before swooping in for the kill is not two different, conflicting tasks, it's a single combat system that gets the player in an perfect flowstate of disabling enemies before they go in for the kill. My conclusion is this: If the artstyle just happens to make you extremely excited then I actually would recommend this game since it does have all its systems in order and plenty of content. It's just that, if you came to Battleshapers because you played another boomer shooter or roguelike and wanted more- you're probably not going to be very impressed, and the fact that Deadlink and Roboquest came out over a year before this game means this statement is probably true for everyone who happens to read this review.

While I would recommend this game, you should know what you are getting. As for me I have very little incentive to boot it up again. PROS: - I personally like the art style and the very colorful nature of it. For me one of the main draws of the game. - Combat is generally OK. - Game runs great. I have a very mid gaming laptop with a 1660 TI. Runs 1440p on High at 60 FPS no problem. The not so great: - I turned off the music after about 15 min. Just some random guitar playing in the background. For me it does not suite the vibe or theme of the game what so ever. - The narrative is very weak, no world building, no personality or any kind of character to anyone really. Feels very much like an afterthought. The random stating the obvious banter I just completely ignored as it did not do the game any favors. - The combat if I compare it to other similar games is just Average. Guns feel OK, not bad, not great. Just OK. The fist punch has some kind of effect where robots will crash into each others. However it's very inconsistent so it did not really feel that great or impactful, you simply have to punch to get your shields. And upgrades are I guess OK. Grenades are very strange as you can't see where you are throwing them and their effect seems very weak in general. - The way enemies just spawn in the room randomly is for me also a bit weird as they can spawn pretty much on you if you moved a little bit before they started spawning in. - The biggest reason for me to not be interesting in playing this anymore though is this: I did 2 runs. Both running until the Boss. Where the boss kills me within the first 30 seconds of the encounter. No time to get into things or even understand the boss attacks etc. However, everything (all of the rooms) prior to the Boss are no challenge what so ever! you Just shoot at everything that moves and you are good. There is also just 1 skill! You have your guns, and the upgrades you gathered. However you don't really have a lot of Kit to play with. Just shoot and use your 1 ability and dash/jump. That is all. For me this game still feels very much early access, even though it is now considered fully released. It feels underbaked and the most playtime you will have is simply shooting random bots until the Boss comes along and shreds you in a few seconds. What is the point of all the upgrades if they hardly matter? Maybe fun if you are into this style of game for 10-15h. For me I have games that are much more refined and more engaging overall. Therefore I'm letting this one slide.

[b]末日洛克铁拳人！[/b] 游戏类型是和死链、机械守护者一样的肉鸽fps，好在本作的常规机动性不高，因此敌人的强度也不算高。 游戏总共四大关，前三关各两层（第二层才有boss）第四关一层共七层，玩家可以自选前三关的攻略顺序，越靠后的关卡强度越高，不仅仅是数值提升，敌人的类型、机关设置、boss的招数也会发生变化。玩家打败boss后可以获得对应boss的能力，这一点就很洛克人，当然也只有这点跟洛克人沾边。 地图设计很一般，分支路线也只是多打一个房间多掉落一两个道具，主路没有太多变化，战斗房中间还穿插跑酷房。 探索做的还行，冲刺、蹬墙跳、重击破墙三个常驻能力需要玩家前期在三大关卡里获得，重击破墙除了找收集用外，打中敌人还可以在战斗中增加枪械双暴。 战斗方面，枪械射击手感有点像守望先锋，可携带两把枪和一个技能（热武器类型挺多，可惜冷兵器并不能近战，攻击方式是蓄力丢出去，这点不如机守），敌人残血时会陷入眩晕，玩家可以使用重击处决，不是doom16那种播动画，是直接一拳打飞（比黑暗时代更超前），被击飞的尸体还能攻击其他敌人，被处决的敌人会掉落护甲。护甲没了才会开始扣血，一般情况下无法回血，只有商店购买、被动强化效果、开起隐藏箱子、挑战失败或者打完boss后才能回血。 肉鸽方面，也是有局外和局内成长，局外有少量的数值提升，更多是增加局内装备丰富度（装备需要玩家现在局内探索收集才能在局外解锁），局内每关打完会随机掉落一个道具（武器、道具或者普通被动强化），每一层最后的房间会固定给一个高级被动强化，然后上面三种道具里选一个。每层结束（boss战前）会进一次商店，可以购买道具或者给当前武器技能升级。部分战斗房会有额外挑战（打精英怪、限时击杀、占点、跑酷、无伤击杀），成功后掉落道具二选一，失败只会回血；部分战斗房里还可能会有一个额外武器或者技能可获得，需要花钱或者卖血。 此外，获得冲刺后可以在序关走隐藏路解锁黑客能力，黑客可以在每一层开头选择一种效果（比如说房间里出现增益、战斗后额外解锁更多道具），只在此层生效，打赢boss后会获得一个高级效果，整局都有效。 虽然游戏里只有一个角色，但实际上开局给主角选核心就相当于换角色了，总共有四个形态，第一次打败任意boss不会给对应核心，只会解锁基础的反射核心，唯一的机制就是大招反射子弹，从第二次打败boss开始才会解锁对应核心。每局可以选一主一副两个核心，主核心会改变重击、大招等，提供专属被动强化，副核心则只提供强化，玩家至少需要击败对应boss两次才能作为主核心装备。 通关一次后解锁更高难度，有点像星界战士，自选减损效果。
6/10，中评，很有巧思的小游戏，像低配版的枪火游侠。但是地图和美术真的很拉，玩的乱糟糟的。武器需要解锁的过多，导致rogue性不算很高。
Might be worth playing if it ran better.

DO NOT BUY. Sweet Baby Inc touched this game. There are a lot of good ideas, but few of those ideas were executed in a manner that makes a game truly great. Far too many systems are locked behind progression, meaning the initial impression of the game is that it's a bland FPS with an unnecessarily tacked-on roguelite skin. Meta-progression is irritating, as whole systems are again locked behind death instead of just adding an increased weapon/skill variety. Boss and enemy design prioritize bullet-sponge over skill expression, and the variety between enemies is severely lacking. Each of the three main bosses are effectively just boiled down to the same attacks with different skins, essentially just 'jump the hazard', 'sidestep the hazard', and 'kill the minions'. Weapons aren't particularly interesting either, you're mostly just going to be using some type of machine gun with an elemental coat of paint put over it. Maybe something will change when I'm deeper into it, but a game really shouldn't take 10h to get good. Edit follows: Nah. It's missing one of the most important things for a roguelite: Excitement. You never pick up an item and think "Oh, this is THE run!" You never get those rush moments because your end of run capabilities aren't much more interesting than what you started with. Depth of a cookie sheet. Also, if you're going to require a 'don't get hit' mentality from your players, you have to have sound and visual design good enough to warrant that level of expectation. If you want to have firing methods based on timing, do NOT slow down actions without warning. You can't demand perfection if you're not going to offer it yourself. Oh and it loses frames like you wouldn't believe once you're anywhere deeper than the first couple difficulty levels. RE2 Remake typically leaves my temps around 42-45c, but Battle Shapers averages high 50s to low 60s, which is unforgivable, given the visual style.
There's battle, but not a lot of shaping.

Battle Shapers is a difficult one to provide a general recommendation for, on the basis that I feel a large portion of this game's design is unintentionally antagonistic to casual players. If, you’re well-versed in FPS roguelites and are looking for something fast-paced and challenging, then I would recommend it, and you’re likely to get 15-20 hours of solid, fun runs. I’ve had a lot of fun and the game was 100% worth it for me - despite what my list below might suggest - but this review is more tailored for those sitting on the fence. If you’re not accustomed to FPS# like this, then it will likely come down to where you sit on the “how much difficulty is enough” scale. [h2] General Overview [/h2] Many reviewers are comparing this to RoboQuest - which is my favourite FPS roguelite - and, to be blunt, this game feels like the dev saw RoboQuest and said: “What if we do that, but different”. The gunplay is similar, the art style for story sections is similar, and the general “feel” when playing is similar, but it doesn’t quite hit the same mark. The game is very repetitive, more so than in roguelites, due to the same map structures, limited-feeling builds, a limited pool of bosses, and the way runs are structured. Start a run → clear a tonne of similar floors/rooms -> beat all 3 bosses → fight final boss. The second video on the store page showcases the gameplay well enough. It really is as it looks - snappy, fast-paced, cognitively demanding, and with a fairly detailed meta-progression system to keep adding new things. So what about this is antagonistic? [h2] The Antagonistic Elements [/h2] The game gets progressively harder, both in the meta sense of making runs more challenging, but also mid-run. If you want to finish the game, this is non-negotiable: you have to keep increasing the difficulty, and it will get harder as the run progresses. On top of this, several factors contribute to that feeling of an inflated challenge beyond sheer skill. Give the below a read and consider whether these would bother you enough to drop the game. If not, I recommend you pick it up. [list] [*] I’ve done 7 runs, and in those runs, I’ve won 4 times and am currently at the final difficulty. In these runs, I haven’t had a reroll. I was given one, but the first tier of difficulty took it away from me, as it was the most logical choice to pick. This happens with other unlocks. Just paid to have reduced trap damage? Nice! Now, how about you get dealt an extra 25% anyway so you can progress. Want more rerolls? Well, buy the machine for 500, then pay more for more rerolls on top of that instead of unlocking things. [*] Continuing on the difficulty element, each difficulty increase requires more of these selected. Unlike, say, Hades, where you fine-tune enemy buffs or your limitations, or even RoboQuest, where each difficulty focuses on increased enemy challenge, here, it’s almost all comes down to making yourself weaker. Sometimes, as already noted, by decreasing things you’ve actively paid meta-progression currency for. So, not only are runs getting harder, but difficulty in mid-runs gets harder (boss locations receive more dangerous buffs), and you’re also getting weaker. [*] My quickest winning run was my most recent at 1:21:45. Longest at 1:38:52. On average, runs are an hour an half. Which [i] feels [/i] too long. Run fatigue sets in real quick at the 1-hour mark when enemies get more spongy, rooms start to blend into one another, and the knowledge that one slip of focus could mean you’ve thrown the run and that time investment. You can leave midway through, but progress only saves at the start of a floor. [*] You get four main cores, which you can think of as classes. The first, I would consider the worst by far, but the others you only unlock after beating the respective boss. then, to upgrade the core and have more build/room choices, you have to continue beating the bosses. Ultimately, this boils down to a slow introduction of arguably the more fun elements to combat, as it takes 2-3 runs to really get the progression started, BUT also means if you’re not someone consistently completing runs, your ability to actually experience this core component of the game takes even longer. [*] Later in runs and higher difficulties, more and more enemies become corrupt, essentially having a shield or element-specific shield. On the one hand, it's cool; it requires you to think about what weapons you’re choosing to get through these more effectively, or just use Kinetic, which bypasses the damage reduction slightly. On the other hand, if you don’t have either, things are a slog. Toward the end of runs, enemies can become so spongy that regardless of what you have, they take ages to kill. [/list] There are also some in-run random things that can also cause frustration. For example, when bosses interrupt mid-room to make it more challenging, your map vanishes, and enemy health bars vanish for seemingly no reason. Additionally, you can’t click and hold to continuously shoot some guns, even if they don’t have a charge? Or if you go to apply a mod to a gun only to find out it won’t work on the gun you want, which you couldn’t know beforehand, you have to scrap it instead of being able to choose another reward. Small stuff, but in the realm of a roguelite, which can get repetitive quickly, the small stuff soon adds up. [h2] Tips if You Decide to Give It a Try [/h2] Nothing really to spoil that hasn’t been shown by the devs. Some random tips I think could come in handy if you want a more streamlined start/time: [list] [*] [b] DO NOT BUY META PROGRESSION ITEMS IF YOU PLAN TO QUIT: [/b] When you finish a run, the obvious thing to do is spend your currency, then quit, right? Well, when you buy skills and weapons, one will drop, so you can immediately use it on a run. If you do this and quit out, they vanish and aren’t there when you next start. [*][b] Ignore the home base teleporter: [/b] You unlock this early, and it lets you skip the introductory rooms. It saves like… a minute or two, and you miss out on 2-3 rewards. Not worth doing. [*] [b] Wind → Strike → Volt: [/b] Will make sense if you play. By far the easiest route for all runs. [*] [b] Don’t buy everything [/b]: Anything you buy gets added to the loot pool. Goes without saying that if there’s something you absolutely wouldn’t want to use (I despise charge-based weapons), just don’t buy it. [/list] And, of course, have fun if you do play!

7,5/10 A very good roguelite shooter strangely similar to Roboquest in its theme. But despite the likeness, Battle Shapers offers a sufficiently different experience. The gameplay is very good, visually impactful and very responsive. There are ranged weapons but there is also a melee attack. And it's well made, I enjoyed the animation, and the slight slow motion when your punch finish off an enemy. And this melee attack is not just for show, it has many usages. The character is also greatly agile. Melee robots, homing bullets, explosions, ... everything can be dodged. The character can dash and wall jump. Aside from rooms filled with robots there are also areas with parkour sections dedicated to these movements. Battle Shapers suffers from the same little flaw as Roboquest, but here it's worse. When the game is launched for the first time, it's very bare-bone. Most of the content must be unlocked, there is only half a dozen of gun, no special ability, etc... Between each run, there is a currency that can be spent to unlock more weapons, auxiliary items (grenade and more) or permanently upgrade your stat. For most items, to be unlockable, you must find their respective data first. They are located in hidden places, or sometimes dropped by robots. Sadly, many of the new weapons unlocked weren't as efficient as the first weapons. There are 4 cores to unlock permanently by fighting bosses. Each time a run is started it's possible to chose between these cores to obtain a special ability (shield, magnetic bomb, etc...) and they can also change the aspect of the other abilities: the punch become a claw, or it can launch air discs, or now double jump is possible, etc... And during each game these special abilities can be upgraded with different modifiers. Even weapon also have modifiers (multi-shot, pierce, etc) that can be switched between weapons. And if the final boss is defeated at least once, it's now possible to add modifiers to the difficulty. Yep, modifiers are everywhere! The second little flaw of Battle Shapers, is that each game doesn't differ much from the previous one. As a roguelite shooter, the random element is not much present. Each game, it's the same four bosses and the same four levels to beat. But the different special abilities and the various modifiers present in every aspects of the game ensure a good replayability. In order to reach the true end the game has to be finished at least 5 times at 5 different levels of difficulty. So there is a story, and it comes with few cutscenes and dialogs, but don't expect something very developed. I had one annoying bug after around 12 hours, which completely reset my story progression while keeping my meta progression intact. In other words, I had to reexperience every dialogs and cutscene from the beginning. The device to spend currency between each game was locked, as was the one for choosing difficulty modifiers. However, I was able to keep my unlocked weapons, stats, and difficulty modifiers as they were before the bug. Finishing the game once more fixed almost everything. By the way, a successful game is between 1h30 and 2h, or less if you ignore the optional rooms, or even less if you die ;)

This game mostly feels uninteresting and uninspired to me. I do not like the core gameplay loop. The fighting and gunplay are solid, but then the platforming puzzles feel pointless and simply suck my health away for no reason. Some of this may be a 3D platforming skill issue, since (1) 3D platforming isn't really my Thing; and (2) there's no way to practice without simply getting through much of the level first. But I'm fairly certain that one of them quite literally had no solution, where, after getting a double dash skill, I had two platform choices, both of which spawned triple dashes away. This platforming feels like the lamest boss fight ever. The music is... not interesting to me. It feels less crafted, and more simply thrown together. This probably goes a long way toward my lack of enjoyment. The cutscenes are awful. I'd rather they didn't exist. The characters feel vapid and I'd frankly be surprised if they weren't AI generated. I don't get the point of this voice grunting trend. Devs want to build in voice acting? Fine. Just text dialogue? Also fine. But text dialogue with grunts? Distracting and off-putting. On top of that, the grunts are mostly cyclic/unchanging per character and poorly voice acted, which, I must say, doesn't feel like the sort of gripe I ever thought I'd post for a videogame. The metaprogression is fine, but it feels extra grindy due to the other issues. I have a few games of this style in my library, and I want to like this game, but every time I see it, I can't kindle that "want to play" feeling. I'd rather spend my time playing any of the others.

Battle Shapers if a Fun FPS Action Roguelike. The story isn't deep, but the game mechanics are. It's Not a perfect game, but it's a Fun game that I jump into whenever I want to relax. You gain new abilities and the progression is paced out really well where nothing gets stale or boring. There are a seemingly endless variety of abilities, upgradeable weapons, and tools to unlock. The possibilities and combinations are well designed. The gunplay and movements are fast, fluid, and fun. At first I didn't know if I would like the art style. But I find it fresh and light. Possible endless replay ability. I picked this up on sale $10, it was definitely worth the price I paid. Very Playable on the Steam Deck at lower setting. Supports controllers just fine. But just like most FPS games, I found it best played with a keyboard and mouse.

I will preface by saying I've never had a game run as smooth and at such great consistent high quality settings on my PC without any stuttering or other issues. Kudos to the programmers for pulling that off. HOWEVER, the game has no idea what it wants to be. The grind to unlock new weapons feels like something straight out of a microtransaction-filled mobile game since the ability to level up your base stats by meager numbers is tied to the same currency you use to unlock new weapons to find on your run. Do you want to have decent health or do you want to be able to use a new gun that you need to buy to unlock? If you want to have both you need to keep replaying the same maps over and over, fighting the same enemies over and over and over, with the same weapons over and over and over, and the random map puzzles can lock you out of loot when you least expect it if you don't have split second decision-making which forces you to memorize different hallways when they spawn so you don't soft-lock your run from loot. On the note of speed, there are times that it feels like the game wants you to go fast because of the timer on your HUD and the existence of dash resets but your momentum is capped. There's barely any build variance for speed and it feels more awkward with their DOOM 2016 inspired takedown system that wants you to melee enemies at low health for shield regeneration as the only base way of healing while slowing down time the moment you do EVERY time you do it without I-frames which, when paired with the awkward momentum, begs the question of how slow or fast this game wants you to take it especially when this play style punishes you for overkilling enemies with your guns which are the main selling point for build construction; another thing this game does horribly. You can choose to rip modifiers from guns to attach to one you have at the cost of losing that gun for either use as is or for scrap (the currency used within a run) which SOUNDS cool until you realize not all modifiers work for all guns. Yes, you can't build a fun build in a genre about making fun builds. This game would have been better if it was a contained campaign like ULTRAKILL with a roguelite side-mode, but instead we get something that distinctly misunderstands why ULTRAKILL, DOOM 2016, and roguelite games are popular. Even with my short playtime, it somehow failed to feel fun to replay despite being a roguelite wherein replaying IS the point. It's by far the worst feeling first-person roguelite I have ever played, and despite how polished it is, it's mechanically terrible and feels like wasted potential.

This game feels weird to me. It is beautiful, and runs incredibly. It's a fast pace fps roguelite, and genuinely feels good. However, there are some problems. The roguelite part of the game isn't roguelite *enough* for each run. There's 4 maps in each run, with each one having semi-random rooms and loot, but there's not enough variance each time you return to provide a significantly different experience. So the first run or two feel really good. Up until you beat the final boss. At which point you realize you're doing the same thing over and over again. You can add modifiers to make the run harder, but that's it. Once you find something that works, you really can just keep doing that thing in each run. The roguelite upgrades are mostly stat upgrades and unlocks, which just doesn't work for the map structure as I said earlier. With the smaller variance in how each run plays out, you really need to be unlocking new traits and abilities. And while technically there is a function for that in the 4 Cores you can equip, those traits and abilities are locked as random loot throughout the run, and the game will provide upgrade options that you just can't make use of without certain other upgrades that you just don't have. Most upgrades either work with a buff/debuff or apply a buff/debuff, but the game will give you the former before you have the chance to get the latter, making that upgrade useless until you can get an upgrade later in the run that actually applies the effect needed. All in all, the runs feel too similar to one another, so even though the combat feels great, it just doesn't make up for the flawed structure of the game. But there is one aspect of the combat that I do want to rag on a little. All weapons have an element assigned to them. Fire, vibro, plasma, or kinetic which is the "no element" basically. Each weapon will be the same element every time you find it, they're predestined like that. The 3 elements inflict a special debuff that corresponds with their element, which is pretty neat, and the elements can interact with each other in fun ways. However, there are random modifiers in the maps that make enemies have a chance to be corrupted, meaning you need to damage them with the according element OR kinetic damage to actually be able to beat them. This modifier sounds fun at first, but it ultimately negates the desire to pick up any elemental weapons. Especially when most kinetic weapons will deal a lot more damage than the elemental weapons? The Devs seem to have made the kinetic weapons stronger since they can't inflict their special debuff, which makes sense. But when kinetic weapons can damage all corrupted enemies and on average do more damage, which lets you negate a modifer in a map while dealing with the ever increasing elite enemies more efficiently, there's just little reason to pick up an elemental weapon. Why would you when in the later parts of a run a majority of enemies won't take damage from it? Each individual aspect of this part of combat works fine on its own, but put all together its just too flawed.

Battle Shapers: Beautiful, Punchy, and Just a Bit Confused About What It Wants to Be. Let me start with the important bit: it's gorgeous. It runs like a dream, looks fantastic, and plays like someone actually knew what they were doing - which, frankly, is a nice change of pace. My mate Johan watched me play for about ten minutes and went "oh, that's lovely," and Johan doesn't say nice things about anything. He once described a sunset as "a bit much." So this is a fast-paced FPS roguelite, and the shooting feels right. That's the part nobody can fake. There are ranged weapons and a melee attack, and the melee isn't just decorative fluff for the trailer. It's got proper uses, lovely animation, and this little slow-mo moment when your punch caves in the last robot standing. Genuinely satisfying. Like popping bubble wrap, but violent and legally distinct from assault. The combat's the good bit, so naturally it's the smallest bit. Fast FPS roguelite, brilliant shooting, and a melee punch with a little slow-mo when it caves in the last robot. Genuinely lovely. You dash, wall jump, dodge everything. Congratulations, you're a gymnast with a gun. Now the catch. For a roguelite shooter, the "rogue" is doing very little heavy lifting. Same four bosses, same four levels, every single run. You unlock stuff with currency - guns, abilities, stat boosts - except you grind for weapons that turn out worse than your starting ones. Nothing motivates quite like a reward that's a downgrade. There's a story, a few cutscenes, some dialogue, but don't go expecting Shakespeare. The 4 Cores are the interesting part, special abilities that reshape your moves. But the good traits are locked behind random loot, and the game adores offering upgrades you can't use yet. It'll hand you the thing that needs an effect long before the thing that causes it. Very generous. Useless, but generous. Then the elements. Fire, vibro, plasma, and kinetic - kinetic being "no element," the beige one. Sounds fun until map modifiers corrupt enemies so only the matching element or kinetic works. Kinetic hits everything and does more damage. So elemental weapons exist purely to be ignored. Every piece works alone; together it's a lovely meal served in a blender. A run's 90 minutes to two hours. Less if you die - no judgement. Still, if you like roguelites, you'll enjoy it. I do, flaws and all — enough to chase the true ending. Flawed and fun beats polished and boring. A lesson Johan's still not grasped about that sunset.
